## Purpose and executable topology
Starward is a Windows third-party replacement launcher for HoYoverse PC games, with launcher, installation, account, game-data, gacha, screenshot, and play-time features. The primary GUI executable is the WPF/WinUI-style `Starward` app, entered through `src/Starward/Program.cs` and `src/Starward/App.xaml.cs`; its main shell is `src/Starward/Features/ViewHost/MainWindow.xaml`.

Supporting executables are a privileged/local RPC worker (`src/Starward.RPC/Program.cs`), an installer/updater (`src/Starward.Setup/Program.cs`), and a native launcher component (`src/Starward.Launcher/Starward.Launcher.cpp`).

## Presentation, composition, and feature boundaries
The desktop client is organized by feature under `src/Starward/Features`. App configuration/service registration is centralized in `src/Starward/AppConfig.ServiceProvider.cs`, while navigation/window hosting lives in `src/Starward/Features/ViewHost/MainView.xaml.cs` and `src/Starward/Features/ViewHost/MainWindow.xaml.cs`.

Feature services own application orchestration; XAML pages/windows are presentation endpoints. Cross-feature state changes are represented by feature-local message classes, such as launch, navigation, and installation messages, rather than direct UI-to-UI coupling.

## Game discovery, metadata, and launching
Game identity and shared HoYoverse contracts are modeled in Core: `src/Starward.Core/GameBiz.cs`, `src/Starward.Core/GameRegistry.cs`, and `src/Starward.Core/HoYoPlay/HoYoPlayClient.cs`. The client retrieves launcher/game package metadata, maps it to supported game variants, then surfaces selected-game state through `src/Starward/Features/GameSelector/GameSelector.xaml.cs`.

`src/Starward/Features/GameLauncher/GameLauncherService.cs` coordinates installation state, authentication/announcements, local game configuration, and process start actions. It is the boundary between UI workflows and local executable/game files.

## Installation worker and IPC boundary
Potentially long-running or privileged game package operations are isolated in `Starward.RPC`. `src/Starward/Features/RPC/RpcService.cs` is the GUI-side bridge; `src/Starward.RPC/NamedPipesConnectionFactory.cs` and `src/Starward.RPC/RpcClientFactory.cs` establish local named-pipe RPC.

The worker exposes protobuf-defined environment and install operations (`src/Starward.RPC/Env/Env.proto`, `src/Starward.RPC/GameInstall/GameInstall.proto`) and executes stateful download, verification/assembly, install, and uninstall workflows through `src/Starward.RPC/GameInstall/GameInstallService.cs` and `src/Starward.RPC/GameInstall/GamePackageService.cs`. This process boundary protects UI responsiveness and separates disk/network package mutation from the desktop client.

## HoYoverse online-data integrations
`Starward.Core` is the typed API client layer, with JSON contexts/converters and service-specific clients. Game record retrieval is centered on `src/Starward.Core/GameRecord/GameRecordClient.cs` and `src/Starward.Core/GameRecord/HoyolabClient.cs`; UI coordination is in `src/Starward/Features/GameRecord/GameRecordService.cs`.

Gacha acquisition is game-specific behind `src/Starward.Core/Gacha/GachaLogClient.cs`, then normalized, persisted/exported, and displayed by `src/Starward/Features/Gacha/GachaLogService.cs` and `src/Starward/Features/Gacha/UIGF/UIGFGachaService.cs`. These integrations depend on HoYoLAB/miHoYo and HoYoPlay endpoints; failure semantics are centralized by `src/Starward.Core/miHoYoApiException.cs`.

## Local user data and auxiliary desktop capabilities
The GUI persists feature data through `src/Starward/Features/Database/DatabaseService.cs`, with gacha, accounts, play time, and screenshot features layering on it or local filesystem/game-process state. Key examples are `src/Starward/Features/GameAccount/GameAccountService.cs`, `src/Starward/Features/PlayTime/PlayTimeRecordService.cs`, and `src/Starward/Features/Screenshot/ScreenCaptureService.cs`.

`src/Starward/Features/Overlay/RunningGameService.cs` tracks running games for overlays and related lifecycle behavior. Native Windows integration also includes URL protocol handling (`src/Starward/Features/UrlProtocol/UrlProtocolService.cs`) and gamepad input (`src/Starward/Features/GamepadControl/GamepadController.cs`).

## Distribution, updates, and runtime dependencies
The installer applies full/downloaded updates and HPatch deltas through `src/Starward.Setup/Services/InstallService.cs`, `src/Starward.Setup/Services/UpdateService.cs`, and native runtime libraries under `src/Starward.Setup/runtimes`. The app invokes update/setup workflows through `src/Starward/Features/Update/UpdateService.cs` and `src/Starward/Features/Update/SetupService.cs`.

The solution targets Windows 10+ and requires WebView2 and WebP support. Builds are .NET plus native C++/UWP toolchains (`Starward.slnx`); release artifacts are published via GitHub workflows, with GitHub Releases, Cloudflare CDN, and SignPath signing as distribution infrastructure.
